name: workspace.status
title: Show workspace status
summary: Repositories of the workspace, which are available and which are variant-independent, where the metamodel comes from, the evidence locations and which are read, read-only state.

name.description: Name of the workspace, from reqseq-workspace.yaml.

repositories.description: The repositories of the workspace file, in its order.

available.description: The repository is on this machine.

path.description: Where the repository lies, as configured: from `.reqseq/local.yaml`, else from the workspace file.

variantIndependent.description: The workspace file marks the repository variant-independent (SR-173): a record without variant for one of its elements counts in every view the element applies in. Left out without the mark.

readOnly.description: ReqSeq cannot write the repository folder itself (read-only file system or no write permission). Reading works as usual and the workspace stays writable; writes into this repository are refused with file.read-only. Rights on the Git server are not visible here (D-016, D-024). Only for available repositories; left out where the operating system cannot tell (Windows).

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the metamodel.

path.description: Folder of the metamodel, relative to that repository.

valid.description: The metamodel was read without errors.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the evidence location.

available.description: ReqSeq reads the folder for evidence: its repository is available, it exists and the reading rules do not skip it (a link, `.git`, `node_modules`, an `ignore` glob, another or a nested repository). `workspace check` says why not.

evidence.description: The `evidence` locations of the workspace file, in its order, as written (#625). Empty without the key.

readOnly.description: The workspace opens read-only because its metamodel is missing or faulty: nothing can be written.
